images.caption: The Storm of the Century (also called the Superstorm of 1993 and the Blizzard of '93) was one of the most intense mid-latitude cyclones ever observed over the Eastern U.S. In this infrared image from NOAA's GOES-7 satellite, you can see just how large and intense the storm was, stretching from Canada to Central America. The storm dropped tremendous amounts of snow from Alabama to Maine, produced extreme winds and coastal flooding, and caused incredibly low barometric pressure readings along the East Coast. In terms of human impact, it ranks among the deadliest and costliest weather events of the 20th century. The one silver lining with this storm was that for the first time, NOAA’s National Weather Service forecasters were able to forecast a storm of this magnitude five days in advance and provide storm and blizzard warnings two days in advance. It was an unprecedented triumph of science, technology and communication.
